target.title: fix(spam-scanner): tolerate comments deleted mid-scan
target.body:
The spam-scanner workflow failed 3x on 2026-07-19 (01:58Z, 03:26Z, 05:26Z). The scanner lists candidate comments, then hydrates minimization state via a GraphQL `nodes(ids:)` batch query. Comments deleted between listing and that batch yield partial GraphQL errors:

```
{"type":"NOT_FOUND","message":"Could not resolve to a node with the global id of 'IC_...'"}
```

`gh` exits non-zero on partial GraphQL errors even though stdout still carries the full data payload (deleted nodes come back as `null`), and the scanner treated that exit as fatal.

## Change

- `src/repair/spam-scanner.ts`: the minimization batch now recovers stdout from a failed `gh api graphql` call (via the existing `ghStdoutFromError`) and parses it; the original error is rethrown when stdout has no parseable JSON.
- `src/repair/spam-scanner-core.ts`: new pure helper `graphqlNodesToleratingNotFound` — drops `null` nodes (deleted comments are simply skipped), tolerates `NOT_FOUND` errors, and still fails on any non-`NOT_FOUND` error type or a payload without `data.nodes`.

## Validation

- New unit tests in `test/repair/spam-scanner-core.test.ts` cover: NOT_FOUND + null node tolerated, clean payload pass-through, non-NOT_FOUND error still fatal, missing data payload still fatal.
- Local smoke run against a fake `gh` that exits 1 on the graphql batch while printing the NOT_FOUND payload: scanner recovers, hydrates the surviving node (minimized-as-spam comment becomes a deterministic candidate), exits 0.
- Lint, format:check, build:all green. Full `pnpm run check` currently trips 8-10 timing-budget tests (git-repo-utils, target-validation, process-tree-containment, action-ledger-runtime) that fail identically on a pristine `origin/main` checkout on this machine — pre-existing/environmental, unrelated to this change.

Closes #111270

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening General Settings in the packaged macOS 2026.7.2 app would immediately crash when the Quick Chat shortcut recorder rendered.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hand-built macOS app did not include KeyboardShortcuts' generated SwiftPM resource bundle. Swift 6.2's generated `Bundle.module` accessor already searches `Bundle.main.resourceURL`, so the package step now copies the generated bundle into the app's `Contents/Resources` directory and fails closed if it is missing. The packager also preserves the committed Swift package resolution byte-for-byte across resolve and build commands.

Regression coverage exercises both the package-script boundary and hosted General Settings construction, so a successful Swift compile alone cannot mask a broken distributable app.

## User Impact

Users can open General Settings and use the Quick Chat shortcut recorder without the macOS app terminating.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the 2026.7.2 failure as a main-thread `NSBundle.module` assertion from `KeyboardShortcuts.RecorderCocoa.configureView`; the installed bundle inventory lacked `KeyboardShortcuts_KeyboardShortcuts.bundle`.

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large base64-encoded images can cause transient memory pressure during decoding. This PR adds a size estimation check before decoding base64 image data in CLI staging, provider image-parsing paths, and the Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route, and propagates the existing configured media size limit through these new guards.

**Security impact**: Defense-in-depth against transient memory exhaustion from oversized base64 payloads.

## Summary

- Reuses the existing public `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` helper (`@openclaw/media-core/base64`) to estimate decoded byte length before decoding
- Propagates existing `maxBytes` limit through:
  - CLI image writing (`writeCliImages`, in `src/agents/cli-runner/cli-images.ts`)
  - Provider image parsing (`generatedImageAssetFromBase64`)
  - **Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route** (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` threads `maxBytes`)
- Boundary tests for configured-limit acceptance, over-limit rejection before decode, default-limit enforcement, and Codex OAuth route oversized-entry drop
- **No new configuration**: uses the existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes` setting
- **No new public package API**: the CLI staging guard is a private function in `cli-images.ts` built on the existing `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` export (per review feedback, the earlier `@openclaw/media-core/base64-size-limit` subpath was removed)

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (final head, 2026-07-19)

Both guarded base64 paths were executed directly on the exact PR head via `tsx` (no mocks — real function calls through the public entry `prepareCliPromptImagePayload`, real filesystem staging):

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/tsx runtime-proof.mts
```

```text
date: Sun Jul 19 2026 08:11:59 GMT+0800 (中国标准时间)
node: v24.18.0
default MAX_IMAGE_BYTES=6291456
code path: cli-images.ts prepareCliPromptImagePayload + image-assets.ts @ PR head
[cli staging valid] accepted: imagePaths=1 file=/tmp/openclaw/openclaw-cli-images/6a2b0d3f….png
[cli staging over-limit] rejected before decode: Base64 payload exceeds size limit: 6295552 bytes > 6291456 bytes
[provider parser valid] accepted: assets=1 mime=image/png bytes=70
[provider parser over-limit] rejected before decode: assets=0 (expect 0)
```

- **CLI staging (`prepareCliPromptImagePayload` → private `writeCliImages` guard)**: a valid 1×1 PNG is staged to a private file; a payload 4 KB over the 6 MiB default budget is rejected by the estimate-before-decode guard with a clear size error — `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` is never reached for the over-limit input.
- **Provider parser (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`)**: a valid `b64_json` entry under the budget produces one asset (70 decoded bytes, sniffed `image/png`); the over-limit payload is dropped before decode (`assets=0`).

## Regression tests (final head)

```bash
pnpm vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts \
  src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.background-tasks.test.ts src/agents/utils/image-resize.test.ts
```

```text
Test Files  10 passed (10)
     Tests  304 passed (304)
```

(Private helpers are exercised through `cli-images.test-support.ts`, the repo's globalThis test-api pattern; `writeCliSystemPromptFile` is imported from `cli-images.js` directly.)

## What was not tested

- Live provider OOM reproduction (neither necessary nor safely desirable). The proof above exercises the exact guard branches on the final head.

## CI note

Earlier-head failures traced to this branch, not main: a stale `../../sandbox/fs-bridge.js` import path, the moved `writeCliSystemPromptFile` no longer exported from `helpers.ts`, knip unused-export findings (test-only consumers), and unrelated `image-resize.ts` churn. Current head: helpers stay private with test access via `cli-images.test-support.ts`, tests import from `cli-images.js` directly, `image-resize.ts` matches main, and oxlint/knip/tsgo all pass locally. Branch is rebased onto latest main.

## Compatibility conclusion — Codex OAuth image-response route (review P2)

Inspected the exact sibling contract in `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`: main already caps the HTTP JSON payload via `readProviderJsonResponse(maxBytes: count × per-image budget)` but decodes **every** base64 entry without a per-image budget; the PR head passes `maxBytes: resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes(cfg)` into `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse`. Runtime contract check on the final head:

```text
date: Sun Jul 19 2026 12:18:44 GMT+0800 (中国标准时间)
route contract: parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse(data, { maxBytes: resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes(cfg) })
[mixed payload] in=2 entries -> out=1 asset(s) (oversized dropped, valid kept)
[single oversized] out=0 assets -> provider throws "OpenAI image generation response missing image data"
[prior contract, no maxBytes] out=1 asset(s), bytes=6295552 (would previously decode)
```

**Conclusion:** the only observable compatibility delta is for individual images exceeding the per-image budget (default 6 MiB, or configured `mediaMaxMb`) — previously decoded (up to the HTTP-level aggregate cap), now dropped before decode; a fully-oversized response now fails closed with the provider's existing "missing image data" error instead of materializing an over-budget image. Mixed responses keep all in-budget images. This is the intended security behavior of the PR; no other runtime contract changes.

target.title: feat(clients): adopt model controls, session management, and keyboard history recall on iOS
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS/web chat parity rounds (#110254, #110276, #110339, #110347) landed all capability in shared `OpenClawKit`, but iOS still only forwarded transport fields: no model controls, no session groups/batch/inspector, no worktree-aware creation, and no hardware-keyboard input history.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adopt the shared surfaces on iOS with iOS-idiomatic UX, keeping the shared API additive:

- **Model controls** (`ChatModelControlsMenu.swift`, wired from ChatPro's existing action menu): provider-grouped model picker via the shared `ChatModelPickerStore` (pinned + recents first, default badges), thinking with `Default (inherited)`, Fast as Default/On/Off (Default patches `fastMode: null`; display rides `effectiveFastMode`; legacy `auto` not re-selectable), verbosity as Default/off/on/full (Default patches null).
- **Session management**: the sessions affordance now presents the shared `ChatSessionsSheet` (groups, select/batch mode, inspector); advanced new-session options (agent, managed worktree, base ref) present in a medium-detent sheet.
- **Transport** (`IOSGatewayChatTransport.swift`): exact-route leases for settings, mutations, groups, and new-session; 6-arg `createSession` mapping `agentId`/`worktree`/`worktreeBaseRef`; settings patches forward the fast-mode double-optional including explicit null. Implementing the real overload removes iOS from the fail-closed protocol default.
- **Input history**: hardware-keyboard ↑ starts recall only from an empty draft; active recall supports ↑/↓; non-empty and soft-wrapped drafts keep native caret movement; no touch-UX change (shared `ChatInputHistory` state machine).

## User Impact

iOS chat users get the same model, Fast, verbosity, and thinking controls as web/macOS, full session organization (groups, batch actions, inspector, worktree sessions from a chosen base ref), and terminal-style input history on hardware keyboards.

## Evidence

- Shared OpenClawKit suite: 994 tests green (48 XCTest + 946 Swift Testing, 81+ suites).
- iOS `build-for-testing` (generic simulator, Xcode project via xcodegen): green — app and test targets compile.
- `IOSGatewayChatTransportTests`: 15/15, including advanced-create encoding, fast-mode set/null, and groups-lease methods/params/decoding.

## What Problem This Solves

Follow-up to #111204, same leak class: when media resolves *after* the admitted user turn already crossed the LLM boundary, the late-media path appends a second user turn whose persisted `content` is literal `[media attached: <path>]` lines. All clients render transcript content verbatim, so users see wire scaffolding under the image.

## Why This Change Was Made

Same bare-storage pattern the timestamp stamping and #111204 established: transcripts persist bare; the LLM boundary projects model-facing text deterministically.

- `buildLateResolvedMediaMessage` now persists bare content (empty string / filtered blocks, keeping real captions and image payload blocks) plus a `__openclaw.lateMedia` marker, protected through `beforeMessageWrite` hooks so a hook cannot silently change provider-visible bytes.
- `normalizeMessagesForLlmBoundary` projects the `[media attached: …]` lines for marked blank turns (`buildLateMediaAttachedText`, same canonical `path ?? url` selection as before); unmarked blank media turns keep the #111204 `MEDIA_ONLY_USER_TEXT` behavior — the two paths are disjoint by the marker.
- History-image pruning runs *before* the boundary, so blank marked turns are materialized at the prune stage too; the scrubber replaces refs with its non-blank marker, so pruned turns never re-trigger boundary synthesis and legacy/marked forms prune to identical bytes.
- Media-field sniffing deduped into a shared `hasPersistedMedia` (trimmed semantics, now also covering `MediaUrl`/`MediaUrls`).
- Legacy transcripts with the persisted literal replay unchanged (non-blank content skips projection).

## User Impact

Late-resolved media renders as just the image (plus any real caption) in every client — no synthetic `[media attached: …]` subtitle. Provider-visible bytes are unchanged across current turns, replay, pruned history, and legacy transcripts. Net −4 production LOC.

## Evidence

- Boundary equality tests: marked bare turns and legacy literal turns normalize to identical provider bytes (string, array+image-block, empty-array-fallback, URL-only, multi-entry, timestamp interaction); ordinary media-only turns still get `MEDIA_ONLY_USER_TEXT`.
- Prune parity tests: marked and legacy turns prune identically without touching real captions; cache-stability suite covers append-only late-media persistence and exact projection.
- Hook regression: `lateMedia` marker survives `beforeMessageWrite`.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound merge-head-diff-base git operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where git operations in the merge-head-diff-base script could hang indefinitely during CI change detection. When git commands encounter network issues or repository corruption, `execFileSync` calls would block without any timeout, stalling automated workflows.

## Why This Change Was Made

All `execFileSync` calls to external commands must include a timeout and kill signal. Without these, transient git issues cause resource leaks and indefinite stalls. This follows the same bounding pattern applied in #109968 (clawtributor GitHub lookups) and #110599 (close-duplicate-prs-after-merge).

## User Impact

Change detection can complete or fail-fast within a bounded deadline instead of blocking indefinitely when git operations are unresponsive.

## Evidence

- Adds `MERGE_DIFF_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` constant and applies `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to both `execFileSync("git", ...)` call sites in `listCommitParents` and `resolveCommit`.
- Pattern consistency: matches the bounding approach in `scripts/changed-lanes.mjs` (#110814).

target.title: fix(plugins): deep-clone registry snapshot so nested mutations roll back (#107514)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The plugin registration transaction snapshot used a shallow clone (`{ ...value }` for object fields), leaving nested registration objects (e.g. hook/tool/config entries) shared by reference with the live registry. In-transaction nested mutations therefore survived a rollback and orphaned registers stayed in the manifest cache (#107514). The earlier shallow clone also collapsed non-plain values (e.g. `Date`) to `{}` on rollback, corrupting typed failure metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the shallow clone with a recursive deep clone that reverts nested data changes on restore. Function-valued fields and other unclonable class instances are kept by reference (registrations carry resolver/handler functions that `structuredClone` cannot clone and that are never mutated), while typed values such as `Date` keep their constructor across snapshot/restore so rollback does not corrupt failure metadata.

## User Impact

Plugin registration install/enable timeouts that roll back no longer leave orphaned registers / stale nested config, and typed registry values (e.g. `failedAt: Date`) survive rollback intact. No behavior change for successful commits.

## Evidence

Real runtime proof against the built module using a real `Date`, real functions, and the real transaction lifecycle (no mocks):

```
[nested-config-reverted]   PASS=true
[date-instance-preserved]   PASS=true
[date-value-preserved]      PASS=true
[function-preserved-callable] PASS=true
RUNTIME_PROOF_OK: typed values (Date) and callable entries survive snapshot/rollback; nested mutations revert
```

Regression tests in `src/plugins/plugin-registration-transaction.test.ts` cover nested-mutation rollback, `Date` preservation, and callable-entry preservation (4 tests passing). `pnpm lint` + `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files.

Freshness gate: `git diff origin/main` confirms the shallow clone is still present on latest `main`; no competing open PR references #107514.


### Custom-class instance identity (re-review fix)

`structuredClone` silently drops custom-class prototypes, so the snapshot helper now keeps typed instances (non-`Date` class instances) by reference when a structured clone would lose the prototype. Real runtime proof against the built module:

```

target.title: feat(durable): add owner-first gateway recovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-running and delegated work can outlive the gateway process that observed it. Today, a restart can leave terminal results or overdue work owned by task, flow, subagent, or session stores without a reliable path back to the parent session. The result is an agent that appears silent even though canonical work state still exists.

This PR adds an owner-first recovery boundary. It projects attention facts from existing canonical owners, persists retryable wake obligations in the durable runtime store introduced by PR2, and only acknowledges a wake after the canonical owner proves delivery or a persistent session handoff accepts it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recovery must not create a second lifecycle authority. Task, managed-flow, subagent, and session stores remain authoritative for their own state. The durable layer stores recovery coordination and delivery evidence only.

The implementation therefore:

- adds explicit `durable.mode` values: `off`, `observe`, and `authority`;
- starts recovery only after the gateway has loaded and published its current config snapshot;
- fails startup before listening when durable authority cannot be established;
- reconciles source-backed attention facts through canonical owner adapters;
- fences session handoffs by session generation and keeps queue rows pending until attached-session consumption is acknowledged;
- reuses existing task, flow, subagent, session, heartbeat, restart-sentinel, and SQLite infrastructure;
- adds no new database tables in this PR.

The earlier fork-only PR3 draft was not submitted. During review, generic registry/executor/worker abstractions and inactive runtime configuration were removed. Inactive human-signal/routes code was also removed, and the subagent lifecycle bridge remains deferred to PR5. This PR contains only production-consumed, source-backed owner recovery.

## User Impact

With durable authority enabled, gateway restart recovery can rediscover overdue or terminal work and reliably hand attention back to the owning parent session. Durable session queue entries survive restart and are not acknowledged merely because they were reloaded into memory.

Default behavior is unchanged because `durable.mode` defaults to `off`. This PR does not claim end-to-end user delivery after every external transport failure; its proof boundary is canonical owner delivery or persistent session-queue acceptance. It also does not add a generic workflow engine or replace canonical OpenClaw owners.

target.title: fix(ollama): bound model pull body reads past idle timeout
target.body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw Ollama setup could hang forever while downloading a model when `/api/pull` kept sending occasional NDJSON progress lines that never advanced useful work. A slow drip resets the per-chunk idle timer on every chunk, so the existing 300s byte-idle budget never fires.

Affected workflow: Ollama provider setup / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` model download.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama setup already aborts if headers never arrive (30s) and already fails if the pull stream goes fully idle (300s). After headers return, the response timer is cleared, so only the per-chunk idle timer remains. Idle resets on every chunk, so a slow drip can keep the download alive indefinitely.

This keeps the headers and byte-idle budgets as-is, then arms a **no-progress watchdog** after the first body chunk. Liveness follows the documented Ollama `/api/pull` StatusEvent contract:

- a **changing** `status` renews the watchdog (status-only compatible producers stay supported)
- aggregate `completed` growth also renews (byte progress)
- **identical** status keepalive without completed growth fails closed (hang floor for stuck drips)
- forever-changing status-only drips are bounded by an absolute **max duration** (default 6h; test-overridable)

Layer progress is keyed by `digest` when present so multi-layer pulls do not overwrite under one status string.

Optional `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs` / `streamIdleTimeoutMs` / `streamMaxDurationMs` on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are for tests only.

Collision check: searched open and closed PRs for `ollama pull stream watchdog`, `ollama pull no-progress`, `ollama setup pull`; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found. The closest closed PR (#99585) bounds native streaming body size, not progress.

## User Impact

During Ollama setup:

- stuck identical-status drips fail with a no-progress error
- healthy / compatible streams that keep changing `status` or advancing `completed` continue
- forever-changing adversarial drips fail at the absolute max duration instead of hanging setup forever

## Evidence

Exact head: `e10932b516ba006acf455d4d4f82e145e74a6cab`

`oxfmt` on touched files — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

We are preparing `@openclaw/gateway-protocol` for public npm publication. Before the surface freezes into public API, this PR executes the "cheat window" cleanup: hard reshapes of protocol families that are provably unshipped (no release tag and/or no shipped store-binary callers), deletion of dead public surface, and durable release-train vintage tracking so future "what shipped when" questions are answerable mechanically.

Shipped-surface audit backing the window (verified against tags + store builds): the `question.*` family is in no release tag; the worker stack / session catalog / durable approvals families are `v2026.7.2-beta` only; native store apps call none of the reshaped families (their "terminal" is a WebView, not RPCs). `tts.speak` and `agents.workspace.*` have shipped iOS/Android callers and are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `question.*`: `id` meant two different things (per-question id and request-record id) and the answers map double-nested (`Record<id, { answers: string[] }>`). Renamed per-question id to `questionId`, flattened answers to `Record<questionId, string[]>`, moved the 12-cap header enforcement to the gateway (TypeBox grapheme semantics) with clamp-not-reject at tool and UI boundaries, and guarded prototype-key ids (`constructor`) in resolve validation.
- Worker stack: converted ~120 lines of handwritten type mirrors to `Static<>`, extracted duplicated primitives into `worker-protocol-primitives.ts`, un-exported/deleted unconsumed schemas, kept placement variants required by generated Swift.
- Session catalog: one shared `SessionCatalogLocator`, `openClawSessionKey` -> `sessionKey`, flattened `SessionsCatalogListParams` (removing the Swift generator merged-union carve-out).
- Dead surface: deleted 55 unused outbound validators plus ~80 zero-consumer schemas/types (verified against consumers, the ProtocolSchemas registry, and generated Swift/Kotlin), added `"sideEffects": false` + pure annotation so consumers can tree-shake, replaced `HealthSnapshotSchema = Type.Any()` with a producer-shaped closed schema, annotated deprecated compat fields.
- Vintage: `since` metadata on all 309 core method specs (precise `2026.7` for this train's families, `<=2026.7` sentinel backfill), `x-openclaw-since` schema annotations, a merge-base-diff guard script wired into `protocol:check`, and a completeness test.
- Rode along: fixed a latent codex side-thread race (late dynamic-tool handlers publishing diagnostics after cleanup) that the reshape made deterministic.

## User Impact

No impact on shipped stable users or store apps: reshaped families have no shipped callers. Beta users of `v2026.7.2-beta.*` worker/catalog surfaces see the new shapes on next beta (breakage explicitly accepted by maintainer). Control UI ships lockstep with the gateway. External consumers gain a smaller, tree-shakeable, honestly-documented protocol surface ahead of npm publication.

## Evidence

- Focused suites green per stage (questions/gateway/harness/ask-user/UI; worker 572 tests + catalog 711 tests on Blacksmith Testbox run 29661844234; gateway-protocol package suite 245 tests; health snapshot suite; since guard + descriptor ordering tests post-rebase).
- Generation stability proven per stage: protocol-gen + Swift + Kotlin run twice with identical diffs; generated models byte-identical for the vintage commit.
- Autoreview per stage until convergence; two real findings fixed (prototype-chain lookup with regression test; header Unicode-semantics clamp), compat-window findings consciously rejected with the shipped-surface audit above. Post-rebase commits reviewed clean in commit mode. Note: full-branch bundle mode trips the reviewer's secret-fragment scanner on pre-existing test fixtures; per-commit coverage is complete.
- Net diff: strongly LOC-negative (worker/catalog −161, dead surface −614 non-test lines).

target.title: fix(doctor): bound legacy session store read with size cap and stat-failure fix
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `readLegacySessionRecords` function in `src/commands/doctor-session-sqlite.ts` reads legacy JSON session store files during `openclaw doctor` with a TOCTOU-prone pattern: `fs.statSync(path)` checks file size (50 MiB cap), then a separate `fs.readFileSync(path)` reads the content. Between the stat and the read, a file at that path could be replaced with a much larger file, causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor migration runs during `openclaw doctor`, regularly invoked by users. While the existing 50 MiB cap is reasonable, the stat-then-read pattern has a Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) race: the stat validates one file's size, but the read may consume a different (potentially unbounded) file. The fix eliminates this window by operating on the same file descriptor for both the size check and the read.

## What Changed

Replaced the path-based `statSync`/`readFileSync` pattern with a descriptor-bound read in `readLegacySessionRecords`:

1. `fs.openSync(path, 'r')` — Opens the file first, obtaining a file descriptor
2. `fs.fstatSync(fd)` — Stats the descriptor (not the path) for size/isFile checks
3. `fs.readFileSync(fd, 'utf-8')` — Reads through the same file descriptor
4. `fs.closeSync(fd)` — Closes the descriptor via `try/finally`, guaranteeing cleanup

All error paths (ENOENT, EACCES, oversized, non-regular file) produce equivalent `store_unreadable` issues as before. The parent-directory validation for missing stores is also preserved.

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `openclaw doctor` with swapped file between stat+read → could read unbounded data | → always reads same file that was validated |
| Only `statSync` on path → TOCTOU race window | → fd pins the inode; race impossible |
| Normal migration with valid files → works | → works (unchanged) |

## Evidence

**All 68 doctor-session-sqlite tests pass (2 skipped, platform-specific):**

```

The descriptor-bound pattern is a standard fix for TOCTOU file races:
- The file descriptor pins the specific inode, preventing substitution between operations

    "legacyEntries": 1,

  }],

    "issues": 0,
    "legacyEntries": 1,
    "targets": 1
  }
}

    "storePath": "<tmp>/oversized-sessions.json",

target.title: fix: catch body cancel rejections in redirect and proxy-validation paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Same pattern as today's PRs #111106 (tlon), #111105 (matrix), and #111081 (tlon): `void response.body?.cancel()` can produce an unhandled promise rejection when the ReadableStream underlying source cancel throws. Two sites in core infra code had this pattern.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `.catch(() => undefined)` so body cancellation failures in redirect processing (fetch-guard.ts) and proxy validation probes (proxy-validation.ts) cannot produce unhandled rejections.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change — body cancel is always best-effort cleanup. Prevents potential Node.js process warnings from unhandled rejections during HTTP redirect following and proxy validation.

## Evidence

- Added a focused test in `src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ssrf.test.ts` that drives `fetchWithSsrFGuard` through a 302 → 200 redirect where the redirect response body has a rejecting `cancel()`. Asserts the final 200 response is returned and no `unhandledRejection` occurs.
- Added a focused test in `src/infra/net/proxy/proxy-validation.test.ts` that mocks the proxy agent/dispatcher and drives the default fetch probe with a response whose body `cancel()` rejects. Asserts the validation result is preserved and no `unhandledRejection` occurs.

target.title: fix(ollama): use CJK-aware char estimate for usage fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama's chat stream reports real usage via `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count`
on the final response chunk. When those fields are missing or invalid (e.g. a
native stream that ends early), `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts` falls back
to estimating tokens as `chars / 4` using plain UTF-16 `.length` on the
message content, tool-call JSON, and tool names.

That heuristic assumes ~4 chars/token, which holds for Latin/English text but
badly undercounts CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) text, which tokenizes at
roughly 1 char/token. For CJK-heavy conversations that hit this fallback path,
usage is undercounted by 2-4x.

This fallback usage feeds `assistantMessage.usage`, which is used both for
usage/context telemetry (`/context`, treemap, totals) and for
`calculateContextTokens` → `shouldCompact` proactive context-window
compaction decisions. Undercounting on CJK sessions means the agent believes
it has more context headroom than it actually does, delaying proactive
compaction until the provider itself errors on overflow.

## Why This Change Was Made

The core already has the correct weighting formula in `src/utils/cjk-chars.ts`
(`estimateStringChars`). Ollama's extension cannot import core internals, and
exposing that helper through the public plugin SDK would create a new stable
API commitment for a single consumer. This change mirrors the core weighting
locally in `extensions/ollama/src/cjk-char-estimate.ts` and applies it on the
production stream fallback path only.

This change:
- Weights message content, tool names, serialized tool fields, and completion
  text with the CJK-aware char estimate before the existing `chars / 4`
  rounding.
- Leaves provider-reported `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count` authoritative
  when present.
- Proves both (1) the production caller path over real loopback HTTP and
  (2) live generation against a real Ollama daemon, including a strip-proxy
  run that forces the missing-count fallback.

## User Impact

No change for ASCII/Latin content (the fallback estimate is unchanged for
that case). For CJK-heavy Ollama conversations that hit the native-usage
fallback path, usage/context accounting and proactive compaction triggering
are now accurate instead of undercounting by 2-4x. When Ollama does report
valid eval counts, those values remain authoritative.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/ollama/src/stream.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/cjk-char-estimate.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts`,
  `extensions/ollama/src/stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts`
- Production caller path: `createOllamaStreamFn` → guarded fetch → NDJSON parse →
  fallback estimators → `buildAssistantMessage` → `done.message.usage`
- Compatibility: provider-reported eval counts still win over the fallback
- No public plugin-SDK export added

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

When an Ollama NDJSON stream's final chunk omits `prompt_eval_count` /
`eval_count`, the production stream path writes CJK-aware fallback usage onto
`done.message.usage` (roughly 1 token per CJK char) instead of the old raw
UTF-16 `length / 4` undercount. Valid provider-reported eval counts still
override the fallback.

### Canonical reachability path

`createOllamaStreamFn` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `/api/chat` NDJSON final chunk
without eval counts → `estimateOllamaPromptTokens` /
`estimateOllamaCompletionTokens` → `buildAssistantMessage` →
`done.message.usage`

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Local `estimateStringChars` mirrors `src/utils/cjk-chars.ts` so the extension
stays inside the plugin boundary without growing the public SDK surface.
Provider-reported eval counts remain authoritative via `resolveUsageCount`.

### Real environment tested

- **Real Ollama daemon**: `ollama` 0.9.6 on macOS arm64, model `qwen2.5:0.5b`,
  listening on `http://127.0.0.1:11434`, Node v22.23.1
- **Case A (provider wins)**: production `createOllamaStreamFn` against the
  real daemon through a same-request pass-through recording proxy.
  `done.message.usage` matched the daemon final-chunk
  `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count` exactly.
- **Case B (CJK fallback)**: same production path through a transparent
  strip-proxy in front of the real daemon. The proxy deletes
  `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count` only on the final NDJSON chunk after the
  daemon has already generated the CJK completion — forcing the production
  fallback. Observed usage matched `estimateStringChars(...)/4` and was
  ~3.8× the naive `length/4` undercount.
- **Harness**: loopback `node:http` Ollama-shaped NDJSON + focused stream
  unit tests (real `fetchWithSsrFGuard`, no fetch mock).

Healthy Ollama almost always emits eval counts, so Case B uses a strip-proxy
in front of the real daemon rather than a fake generator. Generation still
comes from the real model; only the final-chunk usage fields are removed to
enter the production fallback path that this PR fixes.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real daemon (Case A + Case B)
ollama serve
ollama pull qwen2.5:0.5b
# Drive createOllamaStreamFn against :11434 (pass-through + strip-proxy)
# — local proof driver used for the logs below

# Focused harness
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  extensions/ollama/src/stream.test.ts \
  extensions/ollama/src/stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

### Evidence after fix

**Case A — real daemon, provider counts authoritative (same HTTP response)**

```text
upstream: http://127.0.0.1:11434
model: qwen2.5:0.5b
prompt: 用一句话介绍你自己。请只用中文回答。
node: v22.23.1
ollama: 0.9.6

daemon final-chunk counts (same HTTP response):
  { prompt_eval_count: 40, eval_count: 17, stripped: false }

createOllamaStreamFn done.message.usage:
  { input: 40, output: 17, totalTokens: 57, ... }

completion preview: 我是来自阿里云的大规模语言模型，我叫通义千问。
PASS Case A: usage matches same-response prompt_eval_count/eval_count
```

**Case B — real daemon + strip-proxy, CJK-aware fallback**

```text
daemon had counts before strip:
  { prompt_eval_count: 40, eval_count: 33, stripped: true }

createOllamaStreamFn done.message.usage:
  { input: 19, output: 60, totalTokens: 79, ... }

completion preview: 我是Qwen，由阿里云自主研发的超大规模语言模型，具有理解、生成文本的能力，并且在人工智能领域有着丰富的经验和深厚的技术积累。

comparison:
  naiveIn: 5          # old length/4 on prompt + "[]"
  naiveOut: 16        # old length/4 on completion
  expectedIn: 19      # estimateStringChars(prompt+"[]")/4
  expectedOut: 60     # estimateStringChars(completion)/4
  observed: { input: 19, output: 60 }
  inflationVsNaiveIn: 3.80x
  inflationVsNaiveOut: 3.75x

PASS Case B: CJK-aware fallback matches estimateStringChars/4 (>> naive length/4)
```

**Focused harness (production path, loopback NDJSON)**

```text
 ✓ stream.test.ts > falls back to CJK-aware usage when the final chunk omits eval counts
 ✓ stream.test.ts > keeps provider-reported eval counts authoritative over the CJK fallback
 ✓ stream.test.ts > matches the plain chars/4 heuristic for ASCII-only fallback usage
 ✓ stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts > estimates CJK-aware usage when a real Ollama-shaped stream omits eval counts
 ✓ stream.usage-fallback.http.proof.test.ts > keeps provider-reported eval counts authoritative over the HTTP fallback
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a real Ollama 0.9.6 daemon (`qwen2.5:0.5b`):

1. When eval counts are present, `done.message.usage` equals those daemon
   counts (`input: 40`, `output: 17` on the recorded Case A request).
2. When final-chunk eval counts are stripped after real CJK generation,
   fallback usage is CJK-aware (`input: 19`, `output: 60`) — about 3.8× the
   old naive `length/4` undercount, and identical to
   `estimateStringChars(...)/4`.

### What was not tested

- Full gateway `/context` treemap UI and end-to-end `shouldCompact` compaction
  trigger against a long CJK session
- Ollama Cloud / remote multi-host endpoints
- Non-qwen model families (fallback math is model-agnostic; only the missing
  eval-count trigger matters)

### Fix classification

bugfix — usage accounting / CJK undercount

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the local CJK mirror (no public SDK export),
real-daemon Case A/B proof, loopback HTTP caller-path proof, and CI
unused-export cleanup.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body on HTTP error + fix(vertex-adc): guard JSON.parse
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Two fixes in this PR.

1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — Wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message including the file path instead of a raw `SyntaxError`.

**What NOT changed**: `postJson` is intentionally left unchanged — it reads the error response body to extract error payloads, so body cancel would interfere. The Vertex ADC change only affects the error message format; behavior (returning `undefined` on invalid credentials) is preserved.

Fixes #109985

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
- QA Lab HTTP: When `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` receive a non-2xx HTTP status, they throw without consuming the response body. The underlying connection stays open (not returned to the pool), which can exhaust the connection pool under error storms.
- Vertex ADC: A malformed credential file at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` causes a raw `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse`, giving users no indication of which file is broken.

**Root Cause**:
- QA Lab HTTP: `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` call `response.json()` only on success. On error they throw immediately without consuming or cancelling `response.body`. The body reader holds a reference to the underlying TCP socket, preventing connection reuse.
- Vertex ADC: `readGoogleAdcCredentials` calls `JSON.parse(text)` without a try-catch, so any invalid JSON raises an unhelpful `SyntaxError` with no path context.

**Solution**:
- QA Lab HTTP: Insert `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in both `getJson` and `getJsonNoStore`. Optional chaining handles null body; `.catch()` suppresses cancellation rejections.
- Vertex ADC: Wrap `JSON.parse(text)` in try-catch that throws `new Error(\`Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: ${adcPath}\`)`.

## Evidence

### Fix 1: QA Lab HTTP body cancel

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 400: body cancelled 66ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 403: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 500: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 429: body cancelled 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 503: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Null body: safe (no error on missing body) 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Cancel rejection: suppressed 1ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
All non-2xx paths call `response.body?.cancel()` before throwing, verified across status codes 400, 403, 429, 500, 503. Null body and cancellation rejection edge cases are also handled.

**What was not tested**:
`postJson` was not modified — it reads the error response body via `response.json()` to extract an error payload, so body cancel would interfere.

### Fix 2: Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > demonstrates the JSON.parse try-catch improvement 96ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > gracefully handles malformed ADC file via config resolver 3ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
Malformed JSON at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` now produces `Error("Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: /path/to/file")` instead of a raw `SyntaxError`. The `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` caller catches this and returns `undefined`, so `resolveGoogleVertexConfigApiKey` degrades gracefully instead of crashing.

**What was not tested**:
The fix is in `readGoogleAdcCredentials` which is called from two paths: (a) `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` used by `hasGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAdcSync`, and (b) `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders`. Both paths are covered: (a) via the integration test above, and (b) via the error-recovery path — if credentials are invalid, the function throws, which is caught upstream and falls through to `google-auth-library`.

## Tests and validation

### Evidence tests

Both evidence test suites pass at exact HEAD `cab77b1ef899c5734eb4a686873ed880f075cd14`:

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary
- merge-risk: auth-provider — both fixes add defensive guards without changing auth flow or error semantics. The Vertex ADC fix wraps an existing error path in a clearer message; the QA Lab fix adds body cleanup before existing throws. No credential path, token exchange, or provider selection logic is altered.

target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gmail watch renewal could launch duplicate `gog gmail watch start` commands when a previous periodic renewal was still stalled. This affects both the gateway-managed watcher and `openclaw webhooks gmail run` when the configured renewal interval is shorter than the command's two-minute timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Gmail watcher lifecycle now admits only one periodic renewal at a time. Later timer ticks are coalesced until the active command settles, while existing retry timing, failure logging, configuration, and process lifecycle behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators no longer get overlapping Gmail watch registration commands during slow or stalled renewals. Normal renewals continue on the next interval after the active command settles.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` and `src/hooks/gmail-ops.test.ts` — 2 files, 12 tests passed.
- Targeted formatting and lint checks passed for the four changed files.
- Production-lifecycle proof used the real `startGmailWatcher` scheduler and actual child processes. With `renewEveryMinutes: 1`, the first periodic renewal was held for 70 seconds; after 135 seconds exactly two watch-start calls were observed: the initial registration and one renewal. The minute-two tick did not launch a third command.
- An accelerated repeat of the same child-process scenario was captured by the bounded proof runner and produced the same two-call result.
- Fresh open-PR recall found Gmail watcher PRs for delivery mode, OAuth failure handling, secret argv handling, and bind diagnostics, but no PR implementing this single-flight renewal invariant.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): bound az subprocess lifetime on exec timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM`. When the Azure CLI (`az`) hits a network stall during token acquisition, it may ignore `SIGTERM` and block the gateway thread past the 30s timeout — leaving the sync call path hung with no recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adding `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync` call ensures the `az` subprocess is forcefully terminated when the 30s timeout fires.

The async counterpart `execAzAsync` calls `runExec` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime`), not the Node.js built-in `execFile`. `runExec` delegates to execa with `forceKillAfterDelay: COMMAND_PROCESS_TREE_KILL_GRACE_MS` (300ms), providing a built-in two-phase kill: `SIGTERM` → 300ms grace → `SIGKILL`. Source: `src/process/exec.ts:50-63`, `src/process/exec-spawn.ts:7`.

## Evidence Map

| Layer | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Changed surface** | `execAz` in `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts:47-58` — one line |
| **Node.js contract** | `execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM` (Node.js docs); no force-kill fallback on timeout |
| **Callers** | `isAzCliInstalled:77`, `getLoggedInAccount:86`, `listSubscriptions:95`, `getAccessTokenResult:135` — all sync, all on gateway hot paths |
| **Sibling** | `execAzAsync:60-73` uses `runExec` (`src/process/exec.ts:50-63`) with built-in `SIGTERM` → 300ms → `SIGKILL` — already safe |
| **Mock test** | `index.test.ts:591` — verifies `execFileSyncMock` receives `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` |
| **Behavioral proof (sync)** | `index.test.ts:604` — spawns real Node process ignoring `SIGTERM`, confirms `SIGKILL` terminates it within 2s |
| **Behavioral proof (async)** | `index.test.ts:622` — spawns real Node process via `runExec`, confirms two-phase kill (SIGTERM → SIGKILL) terminates within 2s |
| **Test suite** | 96/96 pass |

## User Impact

- Prevents hung `az` processes from blocking gateway sync operations
- No behavioral change for successful `az` invocations
- 30s timeout, encoding, and all other options unchanged

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
Related: #104485

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Crabbox agent commands were forced onto Blacksmith Testbox even when an operator had selected another eligible provider through `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`. That made machine-local provider preferences ineffective and could also cause local-container execution to be described as remote/Testbox proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligns the root policy and both Crabbox/testing skills on one provider-selection contract:

1. Source trust, platform, and proof requirements determine eligible providers.
2. An explicit eligible provider requested by the user wins.
3. Ordinary eligible wrapper calls omit `--provider`, allowing `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` to override the repository default.
4. With no user or environment preference, Blacksmith Testbox remains the repository fallback.

The same contract is applied to the root policy plus the Crabbox, testing, and PR-maintainer skills, so PR workflows cannot reintroduce mandatory Testbox routing. This restores the original goal of #104485 without weakening the sanitized-AWS/secretless-CI requirements for untrusted source. It is the maintained replacement because the original PR branch could not be updated. Original contributor: @hxy91819.

## User Impact

Operators can set a machine-local preference such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container` without changing the shared skill. AWS or another eligible provider can be selected the same way. Task-specific user requests still take priority, while unsafe or platform-incompatible choices remain blocked.

## Evidence

- Current head: `32452922d779597437621cdf63fb02d740b49837`.
- Dependency contract checked in Crabbox source: config files load before environment overrides, `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` overrides the configured provider, and an explicit CLI `--provider` remains the final override.

Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`
